title: A mortality model is evaluated in five retrospective bypass-surgery cohorts
summary: A three-learner ensemble evaluated recorded mortality after isolated coronary bypass surgery. It reported AUCs of 0.9145 in a 952-person internal test and 0.8585 and 0.8553 in two additional hospital cohorts. These retrospective results do not establish a preoperative warning system or improved care.
organization: Shandong University; Nanjing Medical University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Tongji University; Ningxia Medical University

source_review.scope: Original clinical eligibility/outcome/model design and external-cohort discrimination Results;current PubMed bibliographic metadata

evidence.ai_role: XGBoost,CatBoost and LightGBM classifiers were trained and combined as the XCL ensemble to estimate recorded postoperative mortality.
evidence.tested: A 4,764-person pool from three hospitals was split into 3,812 development and 952 internal-test records. Additional hospital cohorts contained 1,733 and 415 patients. The outcome was death within 30 days or during postoperative hospitalization.
evidence.unknown: Inputs include perioperative variables, and an exclusively preoperative prediction time is unestablished. Optimal thresholds used Youden indices; model/threshold comparisons do not establish locked prospective performance. Low event counts, retrospective missing-data exclusions and an Asian cohort limit generalization. AUC differences and decision-curve analyses do not demonstrate clinical benefit or causal effects.
